To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the EGFR exists in a dimeric state on the surface of live cells, even in the absence of EGF ligand, and (2) EGF binding induces a change in the orientation of these dimers, but not in the distance of each monomer from the membrane surface.
the N-terminal domains of EGFR are extended away from the cell membrane in the absence of EGF, and that EGF induces the activation of EGFR within these pre-existing, extended dimers.
the N-terminal tags of the YFP-EGF chimera are extended from the membrane surface and that these tags are within 20 nm of each other in the absence of EGF.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structure of the epidermal growth-factor-receptor (EGFR) and its role in signal transduction.
the molecular mechanisms that underly signal transduction.
the molecular mechanisms underlying signal transduction by the EGF receptor (EGFR), a cell surface receptor that is activated by binding the EGF ligand.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
EGF induces activation within or between preformed extended dimers with little change in the distance between N-termini.

our data are consistent with the model that ligand binding to a single monomer of the dimer is sufficient to induce a conformational change in the dimer which results in activation of the kinase domain and subsequent signaling.

the results of these studies suggest that ligand binding to the EGFR induces activation within or between extended dimers with little change in the vertical separation of N-terminal tags from the membrane surface and thus little untethering of the N-termini.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the N-termini of EGFRs in the absence of EGF are already extended and that the N- termini of EGFR dimers are extended in the presence of ligand.
the N-termini of the EGFR are extended from the membrane surface in the absence and presence of ligand.
the EGFR exists in an extended conformation on the cell surface in the absence of EGF and that ligand binding does not cause a large change in this conformation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a significant amount of dimerization that occurs in the absence of EGF.

we have shown that the EGFR can exist in an extended dimeric conformation in the absence of EGF and that the distance between the N-terminus and the membrane does not change significantly upon activation.
the EGFR is in an extended dimeric state on the surface of cells in the absence of EGF and that EGF binding does not induce a large conformational change in this dimer.
